source_evidence.anchor: Section 2.4 opening paragraphs: Erdős–Rényi model, degree, and the display '(n − 1)p =: d'
source_evidence.observation: The source considers G ∼ G(n,p) on n vertices, defines a vertex degree as the number of incident edges, and sets the common expected degree to d = (n − 1)p.

source_evidence.anchor: Proposition 2.4.1 proof: 'Let us fix a vertex i' through the fixed-vertex Chernoff display
source_evidence.observation: For a fixed vertex i, its degree d_i is the sum of n − 1 independent Ber(p) edge indicators, and the cited Chernoff estimate is P{|d_i − d| ≥ 0.1d} ≤ 2e^(−cd).

source_evidence.anchor: Proposition 2.4.1 proof: 'This bound holds for each fixed vertex i' and the union-bound display
source_evidence.observation: Unfixing i by the union bound over all n vertices gives P{∃ i ≤ n : |d_i − d| ≥ 0.1d} ≤ ∑_{i=1}^n P{|d_i − d| ≥ 0.1d} ≤ n · 2e^(−cd).

source_evidence.anchor: Proposition 2.4.1 proof: 'If d ≥ C log n' through the complementary-event display
source_evidence.observation: For a sufficiently large absolute constant C, the assumption d ≥ C log n makes the preceding probability at most 0.1, hence P{∀ i ≤ n : |d_i − d| < 0.1d} ≥ 0.9.

binders: A graph size n and connection probability p in the Erdős–Rényi model G(n,p). [PDF page 10; printed page 21, anchor: 'constructed on a set of n vertices by connecting every pair of distinct vertices independently with probability p']
A random graph G ∼ G(n,p). [PDF page 10; printed page 21, anchor: 'an example of a random graph G ∼ G(n,p)']
Vertex indices i among the n vertices, written i ≤ n in the proof and summed as i = 1,...,n. [PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: union-bound display]
For each vertex i, d_i denotes its degree, while d = (n − 1)p denotes the expected degree. [PDF page 10; printed page 21, anchors: 'which we denote d_i' and '(n − 1)p =: d']

An absolute positive constant c supplied by the fixed-vertex Chernoff estimate, and a sufficiently large absolute constant C for the 0.9 consequence. [PDF page 10; printed page 21, anchor: fixed-vertex bound '2e^(−cd)'; PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: 'a sufficiently large absolute constant C']
hypotheses: For every fixed vertex i, P{|d_i − d| ≥ 0.1d} ≤ 2e^(−cd). [PDF page 10; printed page 21, anchor: fixed-vertex Chernoff display]

The terminal 0.9 conclusion additionally assumes d ≥ C log n with C a sufficiently large absolute constant. [PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: 'If d ≥ C log n for a sufficiently large absolute constant C']
conclusions: P{∃ i ≤ n : |d_i − d| ≥ 0.1d} ≤ ∑_{i=1}^n P{|d_i − d| ≥ 0.1d}. [PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: first inequality in the union-bound display]
∑_{i=1}^n P{|d_i − d| ≥ 0.1d} ≤ n · 2e^(−cd), and therefore P{∃ i ≤ n : |d_i − d| ≥ 0.1d} ≤ n · 2e^(−cd). [PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: second inequality in the union-bound display]
If d ≥ C log n for sufficiently large absolute C, then the probability of at least one bad vertex is at most 0.1. [PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: 'the probability is bounded by 0.1']
Under that density condition, P{∀ i ≤ n : |d_i − d| < 0.1d} ≥ 0.9. [PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: complementary-event display]
definitions_and_conventions: G(n,p) is formed on n vertices by including each edge between distinct vertices independently with probability p. [PDF page 10; printed page 21, anchor: definition of the classical Erdős–Rényi model]
The degree of a vertex is the number of edges incident to it. [PDF page 10; printed page 21, anchor: 'The degree of a vertex in the graph is the number of edges incident to that vertex']
The expected degree is d := (n − 1)p, and d_i is the realized degree of vertex i. [PDF page 10; printed page 21, anchors: expected-degree display and 'which we denote d_i']
The bad event for vertex i is {|d_i − d| ≥ 0.1d}; its complement is {|d_i − d| < 0.1d}. [PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchors: union-bound and complementary-event displays]
The notation i ≤ n in the quantified event is paired with the explicit sum from i = 1 to n, so it ranges over all n vertices. [PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: union-bound display]
implicit_context: The constant c is the same absolute constant for every fixed-vertex tail estimate; otherwise the uniform factor n · 2e^(−cd) would not follow as written. This is structurally inherited from applying one Chernoff inequality uniformly to every vertex. [PDF page 10; printed page 21, anchor: fixed-vertex Chernoff estimate; PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: 'This bound holds for each fixed vertex i']

No independence among the degree variables d_i is used by the union-bound step; only the individual probability bounds are used. [PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: 'taking the union bound over all n vertices' followed by the sum of marginal probabilities]

The density hypothesis d ≥ C log n is not needed for the union-bound inequality itself; it is introduced only to make its right-hand side at most 0.1. [PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchors: union-bound display followed by 'If d ≥ C log n']

details: The existential bad event is the union, over all vertices i = 1,...,n, of {|d_i − d| ≥ 0.1d}. [PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: left side and summation in the union-bound display]

The all-vertices good event uses the strict inequality |d_i − d| < 0.1d because it is the exact complement of the bad event with ≥. [PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchors: union-bound and complementary-event displays]

The first inequality is the union bound, and it remains valid even though different vertex degrees share edge indicators. [PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: 'taking the union bound over all n vertices']

The second inequality applies the same fixed-vertex upper bound to each of exactly n summands, yielding the multiplicative factor n. [PDF page 10; printed page 21, anchor: fixed-vertex tail display; PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: sum from i = 1 to n and bound n · 2e^(−cd)]

The deviation fraction is exactly 0.1, the failure-probability target is 0.1, and the success-probability conclusion is 0.9. [PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchors: both probability displays and intervening prose]

C is existentially described only as a sufficiently large absolute constant; the source does not give a numerical value. [PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: 'for a sufficiently large absolute constant C']

Independence of the n − 1 incident-edge indicators supports the fixed-vertex Chernoff estimate, whereas the subsequent union bound does not assert or require independence of the vertex degrees. [PDF page 10; printed page 21, anchor: 'a sum of n − 1 independent Ber(p) random variables'; PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: union-bound step]

undebatable_constraints: The union ranges over all n vertices and the displayed sum has exactly the indices i = 1,...,n. [PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: union-bound display]
The bad-event threshold is non-strict (≥ 0.1d), while the complementary all-good threshold is strict (< 0.1d). [PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchors: union-bound and complementary-event displays]
The union-bound chain contains both inequalities: existential probability ≤ sum of individual probabilities ≤ n · 2e^(−cd). [PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: union-bound display]
The factor n comes from summing one uniform bound for each vertex; it is not replaced by n − 1. [PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: sum from i = 1 to n and terminal factor n]
The 0.9 conclusion is conditional on d ≥ C log n for a sufficiently large absolute C. [PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: paragraph immediately following the union-bound display]
The argument does not require the random variables d_i to be mutually independent. [PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: the explicitly named union-bound step]
The source's degree parameter is d = (n − 1)p and d_i denotes the degree of vertex i. [PDF page 10; printed page 21, anchors: expected-degree display and fixed-vertex proof paragraph]

ambiguities.issue: The source does not explicitly state a lower bound on n in Proposition 2.4.1 or in the union-bound passage.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 10; printed page 21, anchor: Proposition 2.4.1 quantifies a graph G ∼ G(n,p) without an explicit n-range; PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: the deduction from d ≥ C log n to a 0.1 bound.
ambiguities.impact: For the usual range n ≥ 2, a sufficiently large absolute C can make 2n e^(−cd) ≤ 0.1 under d ≥ C log n; at n = 1, log n = d = 0 and that deduction does not follow. The exact small-n domain of the terminal 0.9 statement is therefore unstated.

ambiguities.issue: The proposition's prose says degrees are 'between 0.9d and 1.1d' without specifying whether endpoints are included, while the proof gives a strict deviation event.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 10; printed page 21, anchor: Proposition 2.4.1 conclusion 'between 0.9d and 1.1d'; PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: P{∀ i ≤ n : |d_i − d| < 0.1d} ≥ 0.9.
ambiguities.impact: The exact displayed proof conclusion is the open-interval condition 0.9d < d_i < 1.1d; a formal statement using non-strict endpoint inequalities would not be textually identical to that display.

ambiguities.issue: The logarithm base and a numerical value for the sufficiently large constant C are not specified.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchor: 'd ≥ C log n for a sufficiently large absolute constant C'.
ambiguities.impact: Changing a fixed logarithm base can be absorbed into the unspecified absolute constant, so it does not change the qualitative claim, but the source does not determine a specific quantitative C.

contract_plain_english: In an Erdős–Rényi graph G(n,p), write d = (n − 1)p for the expected degree and d_i for vertex i's degree. The preceding fixed-vertex Chernoff estimate says that every individual vertex has probability at most 2e^(−cd) of deviating from d by at least ten percent. Taking the union bound over all n vertices gives P{some i has |d_i − d| ≥ 0.1d} ≤ ∑_{i=1}^n P{|d_i − d| ≥ 0.1d} ≤ 2n e^(−cd). Thus, if d ≥ C log n for a sufficiently large absolute constant C, that failure probability is at most 0.1 and the probability that every vertex satisfies |d_i − d| < 0.1d is at least 0.9. [PDF page 10; printed page 21, anchors: definition of d and fixed-vertex Chernoff display; PDF page 11; printed page 22, anchors: union-bound and complementary-event displays]
